'''''Photinia serratifolia''''' (syn. ''Photinia serrulata''), commonly called '''Taiwanese photinia'''<ref>{{PLANTS |id=PHSE17 |taxon= Photinia serratifolia |access-date=30 September 2015}}</ref>  or '''Chinese photinia''' is a flowering shrub or tree in the [[flowering plant]]s family [[Rosaceae]], found in mixed forests of China, Taiwan, Japan, the Philippines, Indonesia, and India.<ref name=efloras>{{Citation|last=Lu|first=Lingdi|last2=Spongberg|first2=Stephen A.|title=Flora of China entry for ''Photinia serratifolia''|volume=9|page=125|publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden & Harvard University Herbaria|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=242337302|access-date=April 19, 2019}}</ref>



== Description ==
The tree is [[evergreen]], with white flowers emerging in spring accompanied by red-colored leaves, and red fruits growing in autumn. It grows typically {{convert|4|-|6|m|abbr=on}}, sometimes up to {{convert|12|m|abbr=on}}, tall.<ref name=efloras/> Its leaves are toxic due to the presence of [[Glycoside#Cyanogenic glycosides|cyanogenic glycosides]].<ref>{{cite journal | format = PDF | url = http://www.hriresearch.org/docs/publications/JEH/JEH_1996/JEH_1996_14_3/JEH%2014-3-154-157.pdf|journal=J. Environ. Hort.|volume=14|issue=3|pages=154–157|date=September 1996|author=K. A. Jacobs |author2=F. S. Santamour Jr. |author3=G. R. Johnson |author4=M. A. Dirrs |title = Differential Resistance to Entomosporium Leafspot Disease and Hydrogen Cyanide Potential in Photinia}}</ref> The flowers, blossoming in spring, typically last for one to two weeks. Its flowers are known to have a strong scent similar to that of human [[semen]]. The flowers have bell-shaped [[sepal]]s split into five lobes, and around 20 [[stamen]]s. The [[ovary (botany)|ovary]] contains two to four [[locule]]s, with one [[ovule]] in each locule. The tree produces a high amount of bright, red colored fruits that are small [[pome]]s with diameters ranging from {{convert|4|-|12|mm|abbr=off}}, each containing one to four seeds. The fruits, which ripen in autumn and survive through winter, are a food source to various kinds of birds, including [[thrush (bird)|thrush]]es, [[waxwing]]s, and [[starling]]s. The seeds spread primarily through bird excretions.<ref name=efloras/>

== Distribution and habitat ==
The tree is typically found at altitudes from sea level to {{convert|2500|m|-3}}. It is found in mixed forests of central and southern China, Taiwan, Japan, the Philippines, Indonesia, and India.<ref name=efloras/>

==Varieties==
Three varieties of the species are recognized in the ''Flora of China'':<ref name=efloras/><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://frps.iplant.cn/frps?id=Photinia%20serratifolia|title=Photinia serratifolia|website=frps.iplant.cn|access-date=2019-04-10|archive-date=2019-04-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190410070910/http://frps.iplant.cn/frps?id=Photinia%20serratifolia|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* ''Photinia serratifolia'' var. ''ardisiifolia''. Narrow leaf variant native to Taiwan, typically found around 850m altitude. Leaves are [[obovate]] (reverse ovate), ellipse-shaped, and leathery in texture.
* ''Photinia serratifolia'' var. ''daphniphylloides''. Wide leaf variant native to Taiwan. Leaves are [[elliptic (leaf)|elliptic]] or long obovate.
* ''Photinia serratifolia'' var. ''lasiopetala''. Native to Taiwan. Leaves are obovate, slender, or spoon-shaped.

== Uses ==

The tree is widely used as a [[greening]] plant in some mainland Chinese cities, due to the relative ease to plant and maintain, and the tree being less demanding for its surrounding environments. In [[Wuhan]], where the tree is in its native range, the tree is planted by the sides of all major avenues, as well as in the [[Wuhan University]]. However, due to the strong, semen-like odor from its flowers filling the entire city in spring, some Wuhan residents have complained that the tree should be removed and other trees should be planted instead.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.163.com/16/0415/17/BKN9OGS600014AEE.html|title=石楠花的委屈谁懂？专家：它是优秀的园林绿化物种(组图)_网易新闻|date=2016-04-15|website=news.163.com|access-date=2019-04-10|lang=zh-hans}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.changjiangtimes.com/2012/04/385926.html|title=武大石楠花气味怪 砍树?入药? 两不宜 - 长江商报官方网站|date=2012-04-19|website=www.changjiangtimes.com|access-date=2019-04-10|archive-date=2018-04-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180425031904/http://www.changjiangtimes.com/2012/04/385926.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>
